unspecified.behavior: The IntersectionObserver's half-height drawing margin is computed once, when the observer is created (dependencies `[firstRatio, numPages]`). It is not recomputed when the window is resized or the phone sheet changes height. If the first page's proportion resolves while the Pages tab is hidden, the margin is 0 for the whole mount.

scores.reason: After the reader resizes the window, raises the sheet from half to full height, or switches tabs while the document is still loading, pages are drawn only on entering the visible box, or with a margin sized for the old height, so more white faces flash while scrolling.

The margin is not recomputed when the phone sheet changes height, the window is resized, or the reader leaves the tab before the first page's ratio resolves (the hidden scroller measures 0). The only effect is that fewer pages are pre-drawn, so white faces show briefly while scrolling.

The only effect is that fewer pages are pre-drawn, so white faces show briefly while scrolling.

unspecified.behavior: On desktop the outline and the grid share one scroller, so following a distant page (step 9) scrolls the outline out of view when the reader presses an outline row or turns the page in the viewer.

scores.reason: A reader with a long outline who presses an outline entry sees the rail scroll to centre the target page's cell, and the outline they were using scrolls away.

Only PDFs with an outline are affected (none exist in the test drives). On those, pressing an outline row whose page is far down scrolls the shared desktop scroller to centre that cell, and the outline leaves view until the reader scrolls back up.

scores.reason: Fast scrolling through a long document can briefly hold more than 120 rasters in memory. Nothing visible changes.

This only happens after scrolling past 120 pages in a long document. One frame may hold 121 drawn canvases, or more while pages are still in 'drawing', before eviction runs (useEffect runs after paint). The user sees nothing.
